title: Cyclone Names and Climate Risk
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 原文と全九つの学習対象を保持し、日本語記述・翻訳・発展問題を本文根拠のある英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
A tropical cyclone is a rotating storm system that forms over tropical or subtropical water and draws much of its energy from heat released when water vapor condenses. The familiar labels *hurricane* and *typhoon* do not identify two different physical mechanisms. Under the terminology used by major warning centers, both labels can refer to a strong tropical cyclone; the choice depends mainly on the ocean region. In the North Atlantic and the North Pacific east of the International Date Line, the term *hurricane* is used, while *typhoon* is used in the northwestern Pacific.

A regional label is not the same as a personal storm name. Names such as those on annual lists help forecasters and the public distinguish one active system from another. This matters when several storms exist at once: a short, distinctive name can reduce ambiguity in spoken warnings, records, and emergency communication. Naming systems differ among regions, and international regional bodies maintain the lists. The purpose is practical communication, not a claim that a storm has human intentions or a national identity.

Warm ocean water can supply energy, but it is not sufficient by itself to produce a powerful cyclone. Atmospheric moisture, instability, rotation, and relatively low vertical wind shear also matter. Furthermore, a warmer ocean observed during one event does not by itself establish how human-caused climate change altered that particular storm. Such a conclusion requires comparison with a modeled climate in which the human influence is reduced, together with careful treatment of natural variability.

Climate projections must also keep several questions separate. Current assessments find stronger agreement that tropical-cyclone rainfall rates and average intensity will increase in a warmer climate than they find for a rise in the total number of storms. The proportion reaching very high intensity is projected to increase, while changes in overall frequency vary across models and ocean basins. The careful conclusion is therefore not “every place will have more storms,” but “the storms that occur may, on average, carry greater risks from intense wind and rain, with important regional uncertainty.”

questions.prompt: What chiefly distinguishes the terms “hurricane” and “typhoon” in the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: They refer to unrelated physical mechanisms.

options.label: B
options.text: One is always weak and the other always strong.

options.label: C
options.text: They are regional labels for strong tropical cyclones in different ocean basins.

options.label: D
options.text: They identify the nationality of a storm.

questions.answer: 正解：C。第1段落。同じ種類の強い熱帯低気圧を海域に応じて呼び分けます。

questions.prompt: Why are individual storms given names?

options.label: A
options.text: To assign each storm a human intention.

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce ambiguity in warnings, records, and emergency communication when several systems coexist.

options.label: C
options.text: To reveal which country owns the weather.

options.label: D
options.text: To determine an exact future track before formation.

questions.answer: 正解：B。第2段落。地域呼称でなく個体識別によって同時発生時の伝達を明確にします。

questions.prompt: What does “This” refer to in “This matters when several storms exist at once”?

options.label: A
options.text: Using distinct personal storm names to tell active systems apart.

options.label: B
options.text: Giving a cyclone a human personality.

options.label: C
options.text: Proving that only one storm exists in a region.

options.label: D
options.text: Changing the physical mechanism from typhoon to hurricane.

questions.answer: 正解：A。直前の、個々の活動中の嵐を区別するという行為全体を指します。

questions.prompt: What is the role of warm ocean water?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the only condition required for every powerful storm.

options.label: B
options.text: It eliminates the effects of wind shear and moisture.

options.label: C
options.text: It makes all storms follow the same track.

options.label: D
options.text: It supplies energy, but moisture, instability, rotation, and low vertical wind shear also matter.

questions.answer: 正解：D。第3段落。重要なエネルギー源でも、それだけでは十分条件でありません。

questions.prompt: Why cannot one warm-ocean observation alone establish the human influence on one storm?

options.label: A
options.text: Human-caused climate change is necessarily absent from all storms.

options.label: B
options.text: Attribution requires a counterfactual model comparison and treatment of natural variability.

options.label: C
options.text: Storms occur without any atmospheric conditions.

options.label: D
options.text: An annual list of names already supplies a causal experiment.

questions.answer: 正解：B。個別事例の観測だけから人為的影響のない場合との差は読めず、モデル比較と自然変動の扱いが必要です。

questions.prompt: Which projected changes does the passage distinguish?

options.label: A
options.text: Total storm count is certain to rise in every basin, but rain is unrelated.

options.label: B
options.text: Rainfall and intensity are less certain than an increase in every basin’s count.

options.label: C
options.text: Increased rainfall rates and average intensity have stronger support than a rise in total storm frequency.

options.label: D
options.text: No aspect of storm risk can change in a warmer climate.

questions.answer: 正解：C。第4段落。降雨率・平均強度への比較的強い合意と総数変化の地域・モデル差を区別します。

questions.prompt: Which statement is supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The proportion of very high-intensity storms is projected to rise.

options.label: B
options.text: Total cyclone frequency must rise in every ocean basin.

options.label: C
options.text: Sea-surface temperature alone determines an individual storm’s intensity.

options.label: D
options.text: Regional storm labels and personal names are the same classification.

questions.answer: 正解：A。最終段落の非常に強い嵐の割合の予測に直接対応します。

questions.prompt: What does the sentence about “A warmer ocean observed during one event” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: It proves that human activity had no effect on that storm.

options.label: B
options.text: It proves exactly how much human activity strengthened the storm.

options.label: C
options.text: It makes natural variability irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: That single observation cannot by itself establish how human-caused climate change altered that particular storm.

questions.answer: 正解：D。by itself は「それだけで」。影響の否定でなく、個別の因果推定に証拠が不足するという限定です。

questions.prompt: Why is asking only “Will there be more storms?” inadequate for preparedness?

options.label: A
options.text: The number of storms is always the only source of risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Rain, wind, surge, exposure, vulnerability, and regional uncertainty can change risk even without a rise in total count.

options.label: C
options.text: Storm names already determine all damage.

options.label: D
options.text: Preparedness requires a single global number and no local information.

questions.answer: 正解：B。発展問題。総数だけでなく強度・降雨・高潮、曝露・脆弱性と地域差を検討します。
